title: Great Yuan
capsule: The Yuan dynasty was the Mongol-ruled imperial house of China, formally proclaimed by Kublai Khan in 1271 and consolidated after the fall of the Southern Song in 1279, when it became the first non-Chinese dynasty to govern all of China. At its height it controlled China proper, Mongolia, and much of continental Southeast Asia, acting as the eastern terminus of the Mongol world-system and a major conduit for Eurasian trade. Kublai's ambitious campaigns against Japan (1274, 1281) and Vietnam failed, and from the 1320s succession crises and currency debasement eroded authority; the Red Turban Rebellion beginning in 1351 fragmented imperial control, and in 1368 Zhu Yuanzhang's forces took Dadu (Beijing), driving the last Yuan emperor Toghon Temür north into Mongolia and ending the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Yuan territorial extent over China proper is well-documented through official administrative records (hubu registers); control of the northern steppe marches and Yunnan is attested by provincial records, but exact outer frontier lines in Southeast Asia are conjectural, based on tributary relationships rather than administered boundaries.
